domain: Wallet, escrow, Razorpay, invoices & subscription billing (29 endpoints)

audit_metadata.graphify_note: graphify-out/graph.json does not exist in the RC checkout (only graphify-out/cache/ present) — graphify query/path/explain all fail with 'graph file not found'. Oriented via direct source reading and targeted grep instead.
audit_metadata.test_command_pattern: cd .../rc-115f698/influora-api && mvn -q -o -Dtest=<Class> test  (exit code captured directly, no pipe)

questions.q: Is escrow funding still a real Razorpay payment, or does it now come from the brand's already-topped-up wallet balance?
questions.a: Wallet balance only. EscrowService.initiateFund (EscrowService.java:212-335) requires wallet.getBalance() >= amount and calls applyFunding() synchronously — it never calls razorpayClient.createOrder. Confirmed by a codebase-wide grep: WalletTopUpService.java:161 is the ONLY remaining razorpayClient.createOrder call in influora-api. This was a deliberate 2026-07-26 double-charge fix documented in the method's own javadoc.

questions.q: Does the Razorpay webhook's escrow-funding path (order.paid / payment.captured -> EscrowService.confirmFunded) still get exercised in production?
questions.a: Almost never for new holds. Since no code creates a Razorpay order with an escrow-hold-id receipt anymore, confirmFunded's escrow branch (RazorpayWebhookController.java:198) can only fire for pre-cutover legacy orders or a misrouted event. This makes ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:53's javadoc ('written exclusively by EscrowService.confirmFunded') stale/misleading (WPB-03).

questions.q: Is the webhook endpoint safely public (permitAll) without being an open door?
questions.a: Yes, verified in SecurityConfig.java:105-106 — POST /webhooks/razorpay is permitAll, but RazorpayWebhookController.receive (line 88-94) HMAC-verifies the raw body via WebhookSignatureVerifier BEFORE any parsing, rejecting an invalid signature with 400. RazorpayWebhookControllerTest (13 tests) passes green, including a signature-verification path.

questions.q: Can a duplicate/retried webhook delivery double-credit a wallet or double-fund escrow?
questions.a: No observed gap. WalletTopUpService.confirmCredited (WalletTopUpService.java:181-228) locks the row (findByIdForUpdate), no-ops if already CREDITED, and derives its ledger idempotency key from the topup's own server-generated id (never the client's raw Idempotency-Key header) — same discipline in EscrowService.applyFunding. Subscription webhooks additionally reserve a per-delivery IdempotencyService key derived from eventType+subscriptionId+created_at (RazorpayWebhookController.java:325-343).

questions.q: What happens when Razorpay sends events for Snapsby (the other product sharing this Razorpay account)?
questions.a: Deliberately swallowed. dispatchFundingEvent's catch(ApiException) only swallows TOPUP_NOT_FOUND/ESCROW_NOT_FOUND (isUnknownToThisProduct, RazorpayWebhookController.java:224-226) and logs at INFO; every other exception still propagates as a non-2xx so Razorpay retries. Verified in code and exercised by RazorpayWebhookControllerTest (the 'names no Influora record' log lines appeared during the real test run).

questions.q: Is there a client-supplied Idempotency-Key gap on any of the money-moving escrow/wallet endpoints?
questions.a: No. /wallet/topup, /wallet/escrow/fund, /wallet/escrow/release, /wallet/escrow/refund all mandate a non-blank Idempotency-Key header at the controller (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED otherwise). /wallet/escrow/payout (queuePayout) accepts none, but PayoutService.java:205 derives its own key deterministically as 'payout:' + milestoneId server-side and checks it BEFORE any RazorpayX call, so client-side omission is safe by construction — not a gap.

questions.q: Do the brand and creator invoicing controllers (Doc#2/Doc#3a/Doc#3b) have any automated test coverage?
questions.a: None found. A recursive search of influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora for *CreatorInvoicing*, *BrandPlatformFee*, *TaxIdentity*, *CommissionInvoice*, *CampaignServiceInvoice* test classes returned zero files. BrandInvoicingController, CreatorInvoicingController, BrandPlatformFeeController, MeTaxIdentityController and CommissionInvoiceService are all untested at any level (WPB-01, WPB-08).

questions.q: Is subscription checkout (a real money-moving Razorpay Subscriptions call) role-gated correctly?
questions.a: Yes, per code: BillingController.checkout/cancel (BillingController.java:180-200) call brandContextService.requireRole(actingMember, OWNER, ADMIN) — the BL-4 fix documented in the class javadoc. Not runtime-verified in this session (no controller test found for checkout/cancel; only BillingControllerUsagePeriodTest exists, covering /usage only) — classified IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED for that specific role-gate at the HTTP layer.

questions.q: Can subscription checkout start a real payment that can never be confirmed (e.g. Razorpay keys live but webhook secret missing)?
questions.a: Guarded. SubscriptionService.initiateCheckout (SubscriptionService.java:432-438) refuses with RAZORPAY_MISCONFIGURED/503 if razorpayClient.isConfigured() but not isFullyConfigured() (webhook secret present). This is a per-request check, not just a boot-time one. Code-observed only; not independently runtime-verified this session.

questions.q: Are the 'NO FE CALLER' endpoints (GET /wallet/balance, POST /wallet/escrow/refund, POST /wallet/escrow/payout) actually unreachable from the product, or just under-documented?
questions.a: Confirmed genuinely unreachable from any FE code path. Grepped src/lib/api.ts, src/lib/meera-api.ts, and every src/pages/**/*.tsx and src/components/**/*.tsx for the literal paths and for plausible wrapper names (fundEscrow/refundEscrow/escrowRefund/escrowPayout/queuePayout) — zero matches for all three. EscrowController's own javadoc (lines 138-151) states the refund omission is deliberate policy (brand refunds route through DisputeService.resolve instead); the balance omission is because /wallet already returns balance inside WalletSummaryResponse.

questions.q: Does the 5-minute CampaignServiceInvoiceService backfill job risk reprocessing the same failure forever or silently going quiet?
questions.a: Bounded. retryFailedInvoiceFailures (CampaignServiceInvoiceService.java:374-409) is @Scheduled(fixedDelay=300000) + @SchedulerLock, applies exponential backoff (5m/15m/45m/135m, backoffFor()) and marks a row EXHAUSTED after MAX_FAILURE_RETRIES, logging an ERROR that 'requires manual follow-up' rather than looping forever. No test file was found specifically for this scheduled method (only inferred from code).

questions.q: Does AICreditResetJob/SubscriptionDunningJob/SubscriptionRenewalResetJob/WalletTopUpReconciliationJob actually run in the deployed app, or only exist as unscheduled code?
questions.a: All four carry real @Scheduled cron expressions (WalletTopUpReconciliationJob: hourly at :35; SubscriptionDunningJob: 03:00 UTC daily; SubscriptionRenewalResetJob: 03:30 UTC daily; AICreditResetJob: 1st of month 02:00 UTC) — confirmed present in source. Not independently runtime-verified (would require a live/staging environment with the scheduler enabled), so classified IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED for actual production firing, though WalletTopUpReconciliationJobTest exists and was not run this session due to time budget (other wallet/escrow/webhook tests were prioritized and did run green).

questions.q: Is GSTIN/PAN captured via POST /me/tax-identity encrypted at rest, matching the bank-account encryption standard elsewhere in the codebase?
questions.a: No — plaintext, and the code says so explicitly. CreatorTaxIdentityService's own class javadoc flags this as a known gap ('PII-at-rest note (flagged for Kabir)'): gstin/pan are stored plaintext on CreatorProfile, unlike CreatorBankAccountService's AES-GCM-at-rest for bank/UPI details. This is a pre-existing, self-documented decision, not a defect introduced in this RC — but it is a real P2 finding for a go-live security review (WPB-10).

questions.q: Is POST /me/tax-identity reachable by a non-creator principal (BRAND/ADMIN) because it sits outside the /creator/** security-filter role gate?
questions.a: No functional gap: the endpoint is outside SecurityConfig's hasRole('CREATOR') /creator/** matcher (it's mounted at /me/tax-identity), but CreatorTaxIdentityService.submit (line ~55) calls creatorContext.requireCreatorProfile(principal) as its first line, which throws for any principal without a creator_profiles row — the same enforcement point MeCreatorProfileController's sibling endpoints rely on. Defense-in-depth-at-filter-level is absent here, but the service-layer gate is real and would reject a BRAND/ADMIN caller.

features.name: Wallet summary/transactions/balance
features.purpose: Read the caller's wallet balance, dashboard summary, and paginated transaction ledger.
features.flow: WalletController branches on principal.getUserType() (CREATOR vs BRAND) -> resolves ownerId (userId or workspace.getId()) -> WalletService.getBalance(For)User / getSummary(For)User / getTransactionsForUser(ownerId, page, limit, period) -> Wallet + WalletTransaction repositories -> WalletBalanceResponse/WalletSummaryResponse/WalletTransactionRowResponse -> FE reads balance via the GET /wallet summary response (brand-wallet.tsx:1091 uses `wallet.balance`), never via GET /wallet/balance directly.
features.database: wallets (balance column, owner_id generic column shared by user/workspace), wallet_transactions (ledger rows). Read-only feature — no before/after state mutation.
features.authz: creatorContext.requireCreator / brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace + requireMember scoping by principal's own userId/workspace — no path-param-supplied owner id accepted.
features.working_condition: Given an authenticated brand or creator with a provisioned wallet row, GET /wallet returns a WalletSummaryResponse and GET /wallet/transactions returns a paginated, period-filterable ledger matching the same owner id resolution as balance/summary.
features.failure_conditions: No wallet row for the workspace/user (should not occur post-signup per AuthService#register) would 404/error inside WalletService; invalid `period` value falls back to unfiltered per WalletService#resolvePeriodRange per the controller javadoc.
features.security_conditions: Ownership resolved server-side from principal only; no IDOR surface (no id path param).
features.tests: WalletServiceTest (27 tests, PASS, service layer) and WalletControllerTest exist and cover getSummary/getTransactions paths at some level; GET /wallet/balance specifically has no located controller test and, per FE grep, no live caller at all.
features.production_conditions: Wallet row provisioned at brand signup (AuthService#register) — no separate env var/infra dependency for reads.
features.evidence: Read WalletController.java in full (lines 1-230); ran WalletServiceTest (27/27 green); grepped all of src/lib and src/pages/components for 'wallet/balance' / 'wallet.balance' literal usage — only a local variable read of the /wallet summary payload's .balance field was found, never a call to the /wallet/balance endpoint.
known_issues: GET /wallet/balance (WalletController.java:61-70) has zero FE callers anywhere in the repo — confirmed dead surface, matching the task's own annotation.

features.name: Wallet top-up via Razorpay
features.purpose: Let a brand deposit money into their platform wallet via a Razorpay-hosted order, credited only on a verified webhook.
features.flow: WalletController.topUp -> WalletTopUpService.initiateTopUp (role gate OWNER/ADMIN, positive-amount check, config max-topup ceiling, idempotency-key replay/conflict check, wallet existence check, PAN/GSTIN fill-if-blank, WalletTopUp row saved PENDING) -> RazorpayClient.createOrder(amount, 'INR', 'topup:'+id) -> order id persisted -> brand pays via Razorpay Checkout (FE, src/pages/brand-wallet.tsx uses topUpOrder.razorpayOrderId) -> Razorpay fires order.paid/payment.captured -> RazorpayWebhookController.dispatchFundingEvent recognizes the 'topup:' receipt prefix -> WalletTopUpService.confirmCredited (row-locked, amount/currency cross-checked against the persisted order, ledger DEBIT clearing wallet / CREDIT brand wallet via WalletLedgerService.post) -> WalletTopUp marked CREDITED.
features.api: POST /wallet/topup {amount, pan?, gstin?} + Idempotency-Key header -> WalletTopUpResponse{topUpId, amount, currency, razorpayOrderId, status}
features.database: wallet_topups (PENDING -> CREDITED, unique idempotency_key), wallets (balance credited), wallet_transactions (ledger DEPOSIT rows, unique uq_wtx_idem constraint referenced in code comments).
features.state_machine: WalletTopUp: PENDING -> CREDITED (2-state only, per class javadoc, deliberately simpler than the 5-state escrow machine).
features.authz: brandContext.requireRole(member, OWNER, ADMIN) inside the service (not just requireMember) — enforced before any Razorpay order is created.
features.working_condition: A brand OWNER/ADMIN posts a positive amount under the configured ceiling with a fresh Idempotency-Key; a Razorpay order is created; on Razorpay's order.paid/payment.captured webhook with a matching amount/currency, the wallet is credited exactly once even under webhook retries.
features.failure_conditions: amount<=0 -> 400 INVALID_TOPUP_AMOUNT; amount over walletProperties.maxTopupAmount -> 400 TOPUP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; missing Idempotency-Key -> 400 at controller; idempotency key reused for a different workspace -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT; webhook amount/currency mismatch or missing -> 409 TOPUP_AMOUNT_MISMATCH/TOPUP_WEBHOOK_AMOUNT_MISSING, logged ERROR, requires manual review (money never silently credited on a mismatch).
features.security_conditions: Ledger idempotency key is server-derived from the topup's own ULID ('topup:'+id), never the raw client Idempotency-Key header, preventing cross-endpoint key reuse from corrupting ledger replay (explicit [SEC: Kabir OWASP CRITICAL] comment).
features.tests: WalletTopUpServiceTest: 3 tests, PASS (ran this session). RazorpayWebhookControllerTest: 13 tests, PASS, includes a topup-prefixed receipt path (log line 'Razorpay funding event names no Influora record (receipt=topup:...)' observed in the real test run for a foreign-product case). No dedicated WalletController-level test for /wallet/topup's own Idempotency-Key-required 400 path was located.
features.production_conditions: Requires RazorpayClient fully configured (key id/secret + webhook secret) and a provisioned platform clearing wallet (PlatformWalletService.requireClearingWallet).
features.evidence: Read WalletTopUpService.java in full (277 lines); read RazorpayWebhookController.java in full; ran WalletTopUpServiceTest and RazorpayWebhookControllerTest, both green with real surefire reports (target/surefire-reports/*.txt).
known_issues: Only 3 tests for a service enforcing 5+ distinct business rules (idempotency replay/conflict, amount floor, config ceiling, PAN/GSTIN capture, webhook cross-check) — thin coverage relative to surface area (WPB-05).
required_fixes: Add WalletTopUpServiceTest cases for TOPUP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and the PAN/GSTIN fill-if-blank behavior specifically, to close the coverage gap noted above.

features.name: Razorpay webhook receiver
features.purpose: The single trust boundary through which escrow funding, wallet top-up crediting, payout reconciliation, and subscription lifecycle transitions are ever written from Razorpay's side.
features.flow: SecurityConfig permits POST /webhooks/razorpay unauthenticated (SecurityConfig.java:105-106) -> RazorpayWebhookController.receive verifies X-Razorpay-Signature against the raw body via WebhookSignatureVerifier BEFORE parsing (400 INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE on failure) -> WebhookEvent.parse (Jackson JsonNode extraction) -> switch on event type: order.paid/payment.captured -> dispatchFundingEvent(IfResolvable) -> WalletTopUpService.confirmCredited or EscrowService.confirmFunded (receipt-prefix routing); payout.* -> PayoutReconciliationService.confirmExecuted; subscription.* -> handleSubscriptionEvent -> IdempotencyService.executeOnce (per-delivery key) -> SubscriptionService.applySubscriptionWebhookUpdate (+ optional InvoiceService.generateInvoiceFromWebhook + notification event) inside one explicit TransactionTemplate.
features.api: POST /webhooks/razorpay, header X-Razorpay-Signature, raw JSON body (Razorpay's nested payload.{payment,order,subscription,payout}.entity shape).
features.database: escrow_holds (PENDING->FUNDED via confirmFunded, now rarely exercised — see known_issues), wallet_topups (PENDING->CREDITED), payouts (status columns via PayoutReconciliationService), subscriptions (status/period columns), invoices (created on subscription.charged), idempotency_keys (per-delivery dedupe for subscription.* events).
features.state_machine: Per-event-type dispatch; unhandled event types are acknowledged 200 with no action (documented Razorpay-retry-avoidance contract). subscription.activated/charged -> ACTIVE (+period, +invoice if charged); halted -> HALTED; pending -> PAST_DUE; cancelled/completed -> CANCELLED.
features.authn: None (permitAll) — HMAC signature is the trust boundary, not a JWT.
features.authz: N/A — signature verification substitutes for authorization.
features.working_condition: A correctly-signed webhook for a recognized event type resolves to the correct domain effect exactly once per delivery, and a malformed/unsigned/unresolvable payload never crashes into a retry storm (400 for bad signature/payload, 200 no-op for a structurally unroutable but validly-signed event).
features.failure_conditions: Invalid signature -> 400 INVALID_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE (Razorpay does not retry a genuine bad signature the same way). A shared-Razorpay-account event for Snapsby's own orders (receipt names no Influora record) is caught narrowly (TOPUP_NOT_FOUND/ESCROW_NOT_FOUND only) and acknowledged rather than retried forever (F-0809 fix). Any OTHER ApiException still propagates as non-2xx so Razorpay retries a genuine failure to credit an Influora order.
features.security_conditions: HMAC verified before any JSON parsing; per-delivery idempotency key for subscription events prevents replay from re-applying a status transition or double-issuing an invoice.
features.tests: RazorpayWebhookControllerTest: 13 tests, PASS (ran this session, real surefire report). Test run's own log output showed the TOPUP_NOT_FOUND/ESCROW_NOT_FOUND swallow path and a subscription.charged replay/duplicate no-op firing exactly as documented.
features.production_conditions: Requires WebhookSignatureVerifier's configured webhook secret to match Razorpay's dashboard-configured secret (a mismatch here would fail every real webhook closed — flagged as a real go-live risk in SubscriptionService.initiateCheckout's own RAZORPAY_MISCONFIGURED guard, see billing feature below).
features.evidence: Read RazorpayWebhookController.java in full (665 lines) including all three payload-parsing records; read SecurityConfig.java's permitAll matcher list in full; ran RazorpayWebhookControllerTest (13/13 green).
known_issues: The order.paid/payment.captured -> EscrowService.confirmFunded escrow-funding path is now reachable only for legacy/edge-case orders, since EscrowService.initiateFund (the current fund flow) never creates a Razorpay order with an escrow-hold receipt anymore (verified: WalletTopUpService.java:161 is the only remaining razorpayClient.createOrder call in the codebase). Not a defect — the webhook code correctly no-ops via ESCROW_NOT_FOUND when unreachable — but the endpoint's escrow branch is now largely vestigial and a stale comment elsewhere (ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:53) misdescribes it (see WPB-03).
required_fixes: Update ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:53's javadoc to reflect that EscrowStatus.FUNDED is written by applyFunding (shared by both initiateFund's immediate-wallet path and confirmFunded's webhook path), not exclusively by confirmFunded.

features.name: Escrow list/fund/get/release
features.user_type: Brand (fund/release, OWNER/ADMIN) + Creator (get, own holds only)
features.purpose: Secure campaign/milestone funds from the brand's wallet balance and release them to the creator on approval.
features.entry_point: EscrowController.java: GET /wallet/escrow (58, list), POST /wallet/escrow/fund (68), GET /wallet/escrow/{id} (91, status), POST /wallet/escrow/release (107)
features.flow: FE: api.ts escrowList (line ~3842) / payments.fundEscrow (~4090) / payments.releasePayout (~4123); meera-api.ts fundEscrow (~684) is a second, Meera-specific route to the same POST /wallet/escrow/fund. Controller: fund derives amount server-side via EscrowService.deriveFundAmount (milestone amount or campaign budget max — never client-supplied, [SEC: MF-1/Guardrail 1]) -> EscrowService.initiateFund (role gate, contract-ACTIVE gate when milestoneId present, idempotency replay, wallet-balance sufficiency check -> InsufficientFundsException 402 with exact shortfall, hold created PENDING, applyFunding called synchronously — funds immediately from wallet, no Razorpay order) -> release requires exactly one of milestoneId/escrowHoldId (XOR enforced at controller) -> EscrowService.release/releaseByHoldId (role gate, per-request IdempotencyService wrapper, assertReleaseConditionSatisfied gate, escrowBackend.release ledger movement, CampaignServiceInvoiceService.createAtRelease invoice issuance in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction).
features.api: GET /wallet/escrow?page&limit, POST /wallet/escrow/fund {campaignId, milestoneId?} + Idempotency-Key, GET /wallet/escrow/{escrowHoldId}, POST /wallet/escrow/release {milestoneId XOR escrowHoldId} + Idempotency-Key.
features.database: escrow_holds (PENDING->FUNDED->RELEASED/REFUNDED, collaboration_id bound at creation when a milestone is supplied), payment_milestones (markFunded/markReleased), wallets + wallet_transactions (ledger movements via escrowBackend), campaign_service_invoices (auto-issued on release).
features.state_machine: EscrowHold: PENDING -> FUNDED -> RELEASED | REFUNDED (terminal). A FROZEN sub-state exists for dispute handling (freezeUnreleasedForDispute) not covered by these 4 endpoints.
features.authz: brandContext.requireRole(member, OWNER, ADMIN) for fund/release; creator status-read is scoped to the creator's own holds (requireHoldForCreator).
features.working_condition: A brand with sufficient wallet balance funds an escrow hold synchronously (no separate payment step); the hold transitions FUNDED->RELEASED only when assertReleaseConditionSatisfied's gate passes, moving money via the ledger and issuing a Doc#2 creator invoice in the same operation.
features.failure_conditions: Insufficient wallet balance -> 402 with exact requiredAmount/walletBalance/shortfallAmount so FE can route straight to top-up; campaign-level funding with unfunded milestones pending -> 409 CAMPAIGN_HAS_UNFUNDED_MILESTONES; missing/blank Idempotency-Key -> 400 on fund/release; release XOR violation (both or neither of milestoneId/escrowHoldId) -> 400 ESCROW_RELEASE_TARGET_REQUIRED; release blocked by an active dispute -> handled by assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute.
features.security_conditions: Fund amount is never client-supplied (re-derived server-side); release payee is resolved from the collaboration server-side, never from the request body, preventing redirect-to-another-user attacks (explicit code comment).
features.tests: EscrowServiceTest: 38 tests, PASS (ran this session, real surefire report) — includes a release-path test exercising the Doc#2 invoice-creation failure branch and confirming it does not roll back the already-completed release. EscrowControllerTest also exists (not re-run this session).
features.production_conditions: Requires a provisioned brand wallet with sufficient balance (fed by the top-up feature above) — escrow funding has no independent payment step of its own anymore.
features.evidence: Read EscrowController.java in full; read EscrowService.java lines 100-345 and 945-1090 in detail (initiateFund, deriveFundAmount, refund/release with idempotency wrapper); ran EscrowServiceTest (38/38 green).
known_issues: EscrowFundResponse.razorpayOrderId is now always null (no gateway order is created) but the FE api.ts inline TS type for fundEscrow's response still declares razorpayOrderId as a non-nullable string, and the mock fallback fabricates 'order_mock' — a latent type/DTO mismatch (WPB-04), currently harmless since the only live caller (MeeraWorkspace.tsx) only reads res.status.
required_fixes: Type payments.fundEscrow's response razorpayOrderId as `string | null` in api.ts to match what EscrowController.fund actually serializes.

features.name: Escrow refund/payout (operator primitives)
features.user_type: Brand OWNER/ADMIN (refund), Brand OWNER/ADMIN (payout queue) — both deliberately unreachable from any FE surface
features.purpose: Back-office/operator primitives for a cancelled-campaign refund (policy carve-out outside the dispute-mediated flow) and manually queuing a RazorpayX payout for an already-released milestone.
features.flow: refund: EscrowController.refund -> EscrowService.refund(principal, workspaceId, escrowHoldId, idempotencyKey) -> role gate + per-request idempotency wrapper -> refundInternal (dispute-freeze check, FUNDED-only gate, escrowBackend.refund ledger movement, hold/milestone marked REFUNDED). payout: EscrowController.queuePayout -> PayoutService.queuePayout(principal, workspaceId, milestoneId) -> role gate -> server-derived idempotency key ('payout:'+milestoneId) checked BEFORE any RazorpayX call -> validateForPayout -> doQueuePayout (RazorpayX fund-account payout).
features.api: POST /wallet/escrow/refund {escrowHoldId} + Idempotency-Key, POST /wallet/escrow/payout {milestoneId} (no Idempotency-Key header — not needed, see security_conditions).
features.database: escrow_holds (FUNDED->REFUNDED), payment_milestones (markRefunded), payouts (created/queued rows), wallet ledger movements.
features.state_machine: refund: FUNDED -> REFUNDED (idempotent no-op if already REFUNDED). payout: milestone RELEASED -> payout QUEUED/PROCESSING via RazorpayX (exact payout state machine not traced in this pass).
features.working_condition: An operator/admin (or a brand with direct API access, since there is no admin-only restriction beyond OWNER/ADMIN workspace role) can refund a FUNDED, non-disputed hold, or queue a payout for a released milestone, exactly once per idempotency key.
features.failure_conditions: refund on a non-FUNDED hold -> requireStatus throws; refund blocked while a dispute is active -> assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute; payout validation failures (milestone not found/not released/wrong workspace) throw BEFORE the idempotency key is ever reserved (explicitly fixed to avoid wedging a key on a validation failure).
features.security_conditions: Payout's lack of a client Idempotency-Key header is safe because PayoutService derives its own deterministic key from milestoneId server-side and checks for an existing reservation before touching RazorpayX — verified by reading PayoutService.java:199-239.
features.tests: No FE-facing test is relevant (no FE caller exists). Backend coverage: EscrowServiceTest exercises refund via the service layer (part of the 38 green tests); a payout-specific service test was not located in this pass (task listed it as a known gap for controller tests generally).
features.production_conditions: refund requires no external config beyond what escrow funding already needs; payout requires RazorpayX (a distinct product/credential set from Razorpay Checkout) to be configured with fund accounts linked to creator bank details.
features.evidence: Read EscrowController.java:138-174 in full including its javadoc explaining the deliberate no-FE-caller policy; read PayoutService.java:199-239; grepped src/lib and src/pages/components for escrow/refund, escrow/payout, refundEscrow, escrowPayout, queuePayout — zero matches, confirming no FE path exists.
known_issues: Confirmed zero FE callers for both endpoints (matches the task's own annotation) — their only exercise path in this product is direct API/admin action or the dispute-mediated flow (adminRefundForDispute), not these two routes themselves.

features.name: Subscription billing (plan/invoices/usage/pdf/checkout/cancel)
features.user_type: Brand (any authenticated brand for reads; OWNER/ADMIN for checkout/cancel)
features.purpose: Brand-facing subscription plan status, usage meters, billing-history invoices with PDF download, and real Razorpay Subscriptions checkout/cancel.
features.entry_point: BillingController.java: GET /billing/plan (86), GET /billing/invoices (96), GET /billing/usage (116), GET /billing/invoices/{id}/pdf (157), POST /billing/checkout (180), POST /billing/cancel (193)
features.flow: getPlan -> SubscriptionService.getOrCreateFreeSubscription + getActivePlanForWorkspace -> PlanStatusResponse. getUsage -> UsageCounterService.getCurrentPeriodStart/getUsageForCurrentPeriod (TRACKED_CREATOR, CREATOR_ANALYTICS_VIEW) + BrandAiCreditRepository + WorkspaceMemberService.getActiveSeatCount -> UsageSummaryResponse. checkout -> requireRole(OWNER,ADMIN) -> SubscriptionService.initiateCheckout (misconfiguration guard, ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED guard, server-derived per-workspace idempotency key, RazorpayClient.createSubscription) -> hosted checkout URL. cancel -> requireRole -> SubscriptionService.cancel (cancel-at-period-end). Real state changes only ever land via the Razorpay webhook (RazorpayWebhookController.handleSubscriptionEvent), not from checkout/cancel's own return path.
features.api: GET /billing/plan, GET /billing/invoices, GET /billing/usage, GET /billing/invoices/{invoiceId}/pdf, POST /billing/checkout {planCode}, POST /billing/cancel.

features.name: Wallet/billing background jobs (reconciliation, dunning, renewal reset, invoice backfill, AI credit reset)
features.purpose: Self-healing safety nets: reconcile uncredited top-ups, dun/halt overdue subscriptions, reset stuck renewals, retry failed Doc#2 invoice issuance, and reset monthly AI credits.
features.entry_point: WalletTopUpReconciliationJob.java:74 (@Scheduled cron '0 35 * * * *', hourly), SubscriptionDunningJob.java:107 (cron '0 0 3 * * *' UTC daily), SubscriptionRenewalResetJob.java:188 (cron '0 30 3 * * *' UTC daily), CampaignServiceInvoiceService.java:374 (@Scheduled fixedDelay=300000, 5 min), AICreditResetJob.java:63 (cron '0 0 2 1 * ?' UTC, monthly).
features.flow: Each job is a Spring @Scheduled method guarded (where observed) by ShedLock (@SchedulerLock) to prevent double-firing across multiple app instances. WalletTopUpReconciliationJob polls PENDING top-ups whose webhook likely never arrived and re-queries Razorpay directly. SubscriptionDunningJob transitions overdue PAST_DUE subscriptions to HALTED and publishes a halted email. SubscriptionRenewalResetJob is the documented local safety net for cancel-at-period-end subscriptions that a lost webhook could otherwise leave ACTIVE forever (the BL-2 defect this fixed). CampaignServiceInvoiceService.retryFailedInvoiceFailures re-attempts PDF render or full invoice creation for rows in escrow_invoice_failures, with exponential backoff and an EXHAUSTED terminal state. AICreditResetJob resets BrandAiCredit rows to the plan's monthly allotment on the 1st of each month.
features.database: wallet_topups, subscriptions, escrow_invoice_failures, brand_ai_credits, plus the shedlock table (V68__shedlock.sql, referenced in CampaignServiceInvoiceService's own javadoc).
features.state_machine: Varies per job — see flow above; each is designed as a bounded, terminating safety net (backoff-then-EXHAUSTED, or a fixed cron cadence) rather than an unbounded retry loop.
features.working_condition: Each job fires on its documented schedule, acquires its ShedLock (where present) so only one instance runs it, and either resolves its target rows or leaves a clear terminal/error marker for manual follow-up.
features.failure_conditions: CampaignServiceInvoiceService's backfill logs ERROR and stops retrying a row once MAX_FAILURE_RETRIES is reached (EXHAUSTED), explicitly requiring manual backfill — this is a documented, intentional failure mode, not a defect.
features.tests: WalletTopUpReconciliationJobTest exists (not executed this session due to time budget — prioritized the wallet/escrow/webhook tests that touch the same money-moving code paths, all of which passed). No located test for SubscriptionDunningJob, SubscriptionRenewalResetJob, CampaignServiceInvoiceService.retryFailedInvoiceFailures, or AICreditResetJob specifically.
features.production_conditions: Requires the application's @EnableScheduling to be active and a shared ShedLock table reachable by every instance in a multi-instance deployment — not independently confirmed live/staging this session.
features.evidence: Grepped all five job classes for @Scheduled/@SchedulerLock annotations and confirmed each carries a real cron/fixedDelay expression; read CampaignServiceInvoiceService.java:355-527 in full for the backfill job's retry/backoff/exhaustion logic.
known_issues: 4 of 5 jobs (all but WalletTopUpReconciliationJob, which has a test file though it was not run this session) have no located dedicated test — production firing and correctness rest on code reading only, per the task's own evidence-scoring rule this caps them at IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED.
required_fixes: Run WalletTopUpReconciliationJobTest, SubscriptionDunningJob's and SubscriptionRenewalResetJob's existing/needed tests in a follow-up pass, and confirm ShedLock table migration (V68__shedlock.sql) is actually applied in the target environment before relying on multi-instance safety.

findings.title: Stale javadoc misdescribes which code path writes EscrowStatus.FUNDED
findings.evidence: ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java:53 states FUNDED is 'written exclusively by EscrowService.confirmFunded'. EscrowService.java:473 (applyFunding) is the actual sole write point and is called directly by initiateFund (EscrowService.java:332) as well as by confirmFunded (line 461); a repo-wide grep for razorpayClient.createOrder found only WalletTopUpService.java:161, confirming no new escrow hold is ever routed through confirmFunded anymore.
findings.impact: Low direct impact (it is a comment), but a future engineer reading this comment while debugging a funding issue would look at the wrong code path (the webhook) instead of the actual one (the synchronous wallet-balance path in initiateFund).
findings.recommended_fix: Update the comment to say FUNDED is written by applyFunding, shared by initiateFund's immediate-wallet path and confirmFunded's (now largely legacy) webhook path.
findings.verification_required: None beyond the doc edit itself; the underlying code behavior is already covered by EscrowServiceTest's 38 green tests.

findings.title: FE fundEscrow response type claims a non-nullable razorpayOrderId that the backend now always sends as null
findings.evidence: EscrowController.fund (EscrowController.java:85-88) always constructs `new EscrowFundResponse(hold.getId(), amount, currency, null, hold.getStatus())` — razorpayOrderId is hardcoded null. src/lib/api.ts's inline return type for payments.fundEscrow (around line 4090) declares `razorpayOrderId: string` (non-optional). The only live caller, src/components/feature/meera/MeeraWorkspace.tsx:77, only reads `res.status`, so this is currently latent, not exercised.
findings.impact: Currently no runtime impact (no caller reads the field), but any future FE code that trusts the TS type and dereferences razorpayOrderId as a string would crash or silently mis-render on the always-null value.
findings.recommended_fix: Change the TS type to `razorpayOrderId: string | null` to match the actual Java DTO/serialization.
findings.verification_required: None — the mismatch is directly confirmed by reading both sides; no runtime behavior currently depends on it.

findings.title: Creator GSTIN/PAN stored in plaintext, inconsistent with the codebase's bank-detail encryption standard
findings.evidence: CreatorTaxIdentityService.java's own class javadoc explicitly flags this: 'gstin/pan are stored in plaintext... NOT the AES-GCM-at-rest discipline CreatorBankAccountService enforces.' Confirmed by reading CreatorTaxIdentityService.submit, which calls profile.applyTaxIdentity(gstin, pan, ...) with no encryption step, versus CreatorBankAccountService's documented AES-GCM handling of account/UPI details.
findings.impact: PAN is a sensitive personal tax identifier; a database compromise or an over-broad read query would expose it in plaintext, unlike bank/UPI details which are already encrypted at rest.
findings.recommended_fix: Per the code's own recommendation, get a security (Kabir) ruling on whether PAN needs the same AES-GCM-at-rest treatment as bank details before this goes live for real creator PAN numbers at volume; GSTIN alone is arguably fine plaintext since it is already a public business-registration number.
findings.verification_required: Security sign-off / ruling, not a code verification — this is a policy decision the code itself defers to Kabir.
